title: Core Web Vitals Optimization
summary: Improves LCP, INP and CLS with measured fixes to images, fonts, scripts and layout, and reports before and after numbers for each change.
description: Performance advice without measurements is guesswork, and agents are happy to preload everything and lazy-load the hero image. This skill starts from a real Lighthouse or field number, finds the single element or task behind it, and fixes that.
Each change is re-measured. A fix that does not move the metric is reverted rather than left in as clutter.
useWhen: Search Console flags pages as poor or needs improvement
The hero image appears late on a slow connection
Clicks and taps feel laggy on a busy page
Content jumps while the page loads
body:
# Core Web Vitals optimization

Measure, fix one thing, measure again. Targets at the 75th percentile: LCP under 2.5 s, INP under 200 ms, CLS under 0.1.

## Steps

1. Baseline. Run `npx lighthouse <url> --only-categories=performance --preset=desktop --output=json` (and mobile) three times and take the median. Note the LCP element, the longest tasks, and the layout shifts with their sources. Use field data if the user has it; lab numbers alone can mislead.
2. LCP. Identify the element. If it is an image: serve a correctly sized AVIF or WebP, add `fetchpriority="high"`, never `loading="lazy"`, and preload it only when it is not in the initial HTML. If it is text: fix the font (below) and render-blocking CSS. Cut server time to first byte before touching anything else if it exceeds 600 ms.
3. Fonts. Self-host, subset, `font-display: swap` or `optional`, preload only the one or two files used above the fold, and match fallback metrics with `size-adjust` to avoid shifts.
4. CLS. Give every image, video and embed `width` and `height` or `aspect-ratio`. Reserve space for ads and banners. Animate `transform` and `opacity`, not layout properties. Never insert content above existing content after load.
5. INP. Find the slow interaction in the performance profile. Break up tasks over 50 ms (`scheduler.yield()` or `setTimeout`), debounce expensive handlers, and defer third-party scripts with `async` or `defer`, or load them after interaction.
6. Re-measure after each change. Revert any change that did not improve its metric.

## Report

A table of metric, before, after and the change that caused it. List third-party scripts by cost and recommend which to remove.

example.prompt: Product pages have LCP of 4.1 seconds on mobile, fix it
example.result: LCP element was the gallery image, lazy-loaded at 2400 px wide. Changed to `fetchpriority="high"` with a 800 px AVIF srcset and removed `loading="lazy"`: LCP 4.1 s to 2.3 s. Preloaded one font file and added size-adjust: CLS 0.14 to 0.02. A chat widget costs 380 ms of main-thread time; recommend loading it on first click.

faq.question: Does it need a live URL?
faq.answer: It works best against a running build, local or deployed. Without one it reviews the code and marks every suggestion as unmeasured.

faq.question: Why does it revert fixes that do not help?
faq.answer: Each speculative tweak adds complexity to maintain. Only changes with a measured gain stay in your code.

access: Reads templates, styles and build config
Runs Lighthouse and your build; edits images, CSS and HTML head tags
